body:
## Summary

### The problem

In ML, container, and HPC setups, a read-only base image ships heavy, ABI-coupled packages (`torch` with its CUDA wheels, `flash-attn` built against that exact `torch`, `transformers`). Each project adds a lightweight virtual environment on top through `--system-site-packages`, a `.pth` file, or `PYTHONPATH`.

Python imports packages from every `sys.path` entry, and `pip` sees all of them. `uv pip` inspects only the virtual environment's own `site-packages`. When a user installs an upper-layer package such as `torchmetrics`, `uv pip install` misses the base `torch`, downloads gigabytes of duplicate `torch` and CUDA wheels into the virtual environment, shadows the base `torch`, and can break prebuilt C++/CUDA extensions in the base image:

```text
Layered setup (--system-site-packages or .pth):
  sys.path[1]  .venv/.../site-packages            (mutable project venv)
  sys.path[2]  /pre-installed/.../site-packages   (read-only image: torch 2.15 + CUDA,
                                                   flash-attn built against that torch)

uv pip install torchmetrics  (requires torch>=2.0):

  Today (uv inspects sys.path[1] only):
    misses torch in [2] --> installs 33 wheels (new torch + 18 cuda/nvidia wheels) into [1]
                        --> [1]/torch shadows [2]/torch
                        --> [2]/flash_attn can fail to import if [1]/torch differs
                            from the torch it was built against  [X]

  With UV_PREVIEW_FEATURES=sys-path-discovery:
    scans [1] (mutable) + [2] (read-only) --> [2]/torch satisfies torch>=2.0
                                          --> installs 3 wheels into [1] (torchmetrics,
                                              lightning-utilities, packaging)
                                          --> Python keeps [2]/torch + [2]/flash_attn  [OK]
```

### Proposed solution

Add an opt-in preview feature, `sys-path-discovery`, scoped strictly to `uv pip` inspection and additive install commands (`list`, `freeze`, `show`, `tree`, `check`, `install`, `uninstall`):

1. **Discover packages from the runtime `sys.path`:** `uv` runs `python -B -c` (without `-I`, after dropping `''` so a local `json.py` cannot execute) to read the interpreter's live `sys.path` in import order. This covers `--system-site-packages`, `.pth` files, `sitecustomize.py`, `PYTHONPATH`, Debian `dist-packages`, and Fedora `lib64` without re-implementing Python's `site` rules. `uv` already uses `.pth` layering for `uv run --with` overlays (#15121).
2. **Treat directories outside the environment as read-only:** Only the target environment's `purelib` and `platlib` are mutable. Packages on other `sys.path` entries satisfy requirements, can be shadowed in the environment when a different version is requested, and are never uninstalled. If a read-only entry precedes the environment on `sys.path` (for example via `PYTHONPATH`), installing a new copy fails instead of writing files that Python would never import.

### Why this narrow scope can succeed

Users have asked for layered `sys.path` support since #2500 (March 2024) across at least eight issues. Two PRs (#9849, #11670) came close without merging because solving this across all of `uv` at once hits hard conflicts with lockfiles, uninstallation, and interpreter caching.

This proposal implements the narrower first step that konstin and danielhollas converged on in #2500 ([1](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/issues/2500#issuecomment-3200466445), [2](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/issues/2500#issuecomment-3200529787)). That scope sidesteps each earlier blocker:

- **No lockfile or `sync` conflict:** `uv pip sync`, `uv sync`, `uv lock`, and project, tool, and build environments stay out of scope. Lockfiles pin exact versions and expect to remove extraneous packages, which conflicts with read-only base layers.
- **No uninstall of base packages:** Inherited packages are read-only. `uv pip uninstall` warns and skips them, matching `pip` (`Not uninstalling <pkg> at <path>, outside environment <venv>`).
- **No interpreter-cache staleness (#18510, #21960):** `.pth` files and `PYTHONPATH` change `sys.path` without touching the Python executable, which blocked caching inherited packages in interpreter metadata (#21960). Querying `sys.path` per command only when `sys-path-discovery` is enabled avoids stale cache keys and leaves default `uv` at zero overhead (with 300 inherited distributions on a debug build, `uv pip list` takes 22 ms by default and 74 ms with the preview).
- **Small, isolated code change with offline tests:** One helper in `uv-pip-commands` gates the mode; all existing `SitePackages` callers keep scheme discovery. A working prototype (https://github.com/Hangzhi/uv/pull/1) implements this in **+323/−26 lines of production Rust** and **289 lines of offline `.pth`/`PYTHONPATH` tests** that require no fake system interpreter (+635/−27 total in 20 files, vs. +1,308/−260 in #11670).

## Example

`/pre-installed/python3` is a root-owned CPython 3.12 with `torch` 2.15.0 and its CUDA wheels (31 distributions, 5.2 GB):

```console
$ uv venv --system-site-packages --python /pre-installed/python3/bin/python3
$ export UV_PREVIEW_FEATURES=sys-path-discovery
```

| Command | uv today | With `sys-path-discovery` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `uv pip show torch` | `warning: Package(s) not found for: torch` | `Location: /pre-installed/python3/lib/python3.12/site-packages` |
| `uv pip install torchmetrics` | Would install 33 packages, including `torch`, `triton`, and 18 `cuda-*` and `nvidia-*` wheels | Installs 3 packages: `lightning-utilities`, `packaging`, `torchmetrics` |
| `uv pip uninstall torch` | `warning: Skipping torch as it is not installed` | `warning: Skipping torch as it is installed in a read-only location: /pre-installed/python3/lib/python3.12/site-packages/torch-2.15.0.dist-info` |

After the install, Python still imports `torch` from `/pre-installed/python3`.

Demo of this example with a release build of the prototype on Linux x86_64 (48 s):

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/66fb57d3-9be3-4a5a-8d40-5929f8c94cbe

## Proposed behavior

| Scenario | uv today | With `sys-path-discovery` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `uv pip list`, `freeze`, `show`, `tree`, `check` | Environment `site-packages` only | Every `sys.path` entry, with each package's real location |
| `uv pip install foo`, and an inherited `foo` satisfies it | Installs `foo` again | `Checked 1 package` |
| `uv pip install foo==2.0`, and the inherited `foo` is 1.0 | Installs `foo` 2.0 into the environment | Same. The environment copy shadows the inherited copy, and `uv` never removes the inherited copy. |
| A read-only `foo` precedes the environment on `sys.path` | Installs a copy that Python never imports | Error: `Cannot install foo because the read-only installation at <path> precedes the environment on sys.path` |
| `uv pip install --exact` | Removes environment packages that the request doesn't list | Same. Inherited packages are never extraneous. |
| `uv pip uninstall foo`, and only an inherited `foo` exists | `warning: Skipping foo as it is not installed` | `warning: Skipping foo as it is installed in a read-only location: <path>` |
| `uv pip sync`, `uv sync`, `uv lock`, project, tool, and build environments | Environment `site-packages` only | Unchanged (`--target` and `--prefix` also skip the query) |

## Prior attempts

| PR | Approach | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #9849 (pradyunsg, 2024-12) | Use `sys.path` for package discovery; uninstall changes still TODO | Draft, no update since 2025-04 |
| #11670 (konstin, 2025-02) | Read-only inherited packages from the runtime `sys.path`, including `sync`: +1,308/−260 in 26 files | Closed without merge on 2026-06-23 |
| #21960 (konstin, 2026-09) | Keep base `site-packages` in interpreter metadata for new environments | Closed without merge ("Doesn't make sense without doing caching first") |
| #15121 (zanieb, 2025-08) | Include all `site-packages` directories in `uv run --with` overlays | Merged |

## Prototype

https://github.com/Hangzhi/uv/pull/1 keeps the read-only model of #11670 behind `UV_PREVIEW_FEATURES=sys-path-discovery` and applies it only to `uv pip` (+635/−27 in 20 files). Seven offline integration tests cover `.pth` layers, `PYTHONPATH` layers, satisfied installs, shadowing, the unshadowable-precedence error, `--exact`, and read-only uninstall. A release build ran the `torch` example above end to end on Linux x86_64; macOS and Windows have not been tested yet.

## Questions

1. Full `sys.path`, or an explicit list of read-only paths? konstin suggested specific paths first. Full `sys.path` avoids re-deriving `.pth` and `sitecustomize` effects; an explicit path option could follow for callers that want narrower control.
2. On a version mismatch, should `uv` shadow the inherited copy (as `pip` does) or fail? The prototype shadows.
3. Do you agree that we should ship this support for `uv pip` first, and leave `uv sync` and project commands for a later discussion?
title: Opt-in, read-only discovery of inherited packages on `sys.path` for `uv pip`
